thread:
nina (PM): Heads-up: LedgerCo wants a commitment on interactive chat latency for their pilot. Their bar: P95 < 120ms for user-facing sessions. This is a potential Dedicated sale but we need to decide scope fast.
edo (Eng): 120ms P95 is pretty tight. Two ways: surgical infra+routing changes (low dev risk) or deep runtime/kernel changes (high dev risk). Which track do we score?
lucy (ML): Also depends heavily on session seq length and token reuse. If they have many short sessions, routing+prewarm can win. If they stream long docs, only kernel/quantization helps. Need traces.
raj (SRE): Ops constraints: dedicated pool + active pre-warm or warm standby. That increases baseline cost. Finance will want a delta estimate.
claire (Finance): If this becomes a Dedicated contract we need rough delta: estimate +15% infra vs baseline for warm pools, +40-60% if we buy reserved capacity. Numbers matter for ROI.
nina (PM): Let's use a quick RICE-style calc to help leadership pick. Proposal: Reach=1 (pilot customer), Impact=8 (close + reference), Confidence=5, Effort options: Track 1 (routing+cache)=3, Track 2 (runtime)=9. Any objections?
edo (Eng): Fine. But split effort: small-scope MVP (tracking flags, hotspot routing, prewarm) is 2-3 dev-weeks. Full runtime perf is months.
lucy (ML): I'll run a 72h trace analysis today. If prefix hit >50% we can be confident Track 1 will reach ~70% tail reduction. I'll post numbers with sample command: `POST /telemetry/query {"slice":"ledgerco-chat","range":"72h"}`
raj (SRE): Risk callout: routing to low-latency pool creates tail variance if warm pool is saturated. We need autoscaler headroom and a fallback policy (route to standard pool with degraded SLA).
nina (PM): Proposed launch criteria for the pilot: 1) P95 < 120ms for LedgerCo's slice over a 7-day rolling window, 2) infra cost delta < 25% for pilot, 3) automatic failover with SLA downgrade documented. Agree?
lucy (ML): Agree, but add telemetry requirement: produce per-request trace IDs and percent of KV cache hits during pilot. That data is needed to justify next steps.
edo (Eng): Implementation plan (short): feature flag `ledgerco_lowlatency=true`, route policy `prefer_warm_pool`, prewarm N=3 per node. We'll canary behind feature flag.
claire (Finance): If pilot pricing includes a success-based bump, we need cost model and expected uplift. Sales can take risk if upside > $300k ARR.
nina (PM): Ops-bot, please create ticket and add the PRD skeleton and RICE table.
ops-bot: Ticket created: PROD-1420 "LedgerCo low-latency pilot"  assignees: nina, edo, lucy  due: 2026-04-17.
raj (SRE): Vote check: prioritize Track 1 (routing+cache+prewarm) for next sprint. React :thumbsup: to approve.
edo (Eng): :thumbsup:
lucy (ML): :thumbsup:
claire (Finance): :thumbsup: (pending cost model)
nina (PM): OK green. Next steps: - Lucy posts trace summary in 24h - Edo posts a 2-week plan and risk list by EOD Friday in #eng-runtime - Nina will draft PRD with explicit RICE table and launch gates, link PROD-1420.
edo (Eng): If trace shows low prefix reuse, fallback plan is to tune batching and reduce max seq length or consider a model variant that supports faster decode. That increases effort but still cheaper than full runtime rewrite.
lucy (ML): I'll include a breakdown: prefix hit rate, median seq length, percent of requests >512 tokens. That will drive the confidence field in RICE.
nina (PM): Thanks everyone. We'll use RICE but emphasize sequencing: ship Track 1 fast to de-risk and only invest in Track 2 if metrics show remaining tail issues. Reconvene after Lucy posts. :rocket:
